## Body

BLOCK -- R1, exact head ad27621c0f995aaf4cafcd9937257ebc84018c09.

The cross-process crash fix is supported by independent green and mutation evidence. One scoped correctness defect remains: the new acquisition wait blocks async runtime workers. This agrees with performance finding P280-001; it is not a second demand to redesign the existing fork fallback.

## R280-001 / P280-001: contended acquisition blocks the executor

`PaneObserver::start` uses `tokio::spawn` (`crates/daemon/src/pane_observer.rs:202-218`), and `observe_once:247` awaits the directly composed real adapter. `TmuxAdapter::list_panes` (`crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:870-874`) calls synchronous `stdout:469-473`, then `ControlClient::ask/start` (`crates/tmux/src/control.rs:281-304,343-347`). `lock_attach:459` repeatedly calls `std::thread::sleep` while the caller holds `Mutex<State>`. There is no blocking-pool boundary.

An isolated diagnostic at this head, using a cooperating held attach lock and the real adapter on a current-thread Tokio runtime, measured:

- First fallback read: 3.255892291 seconds.
- An independently armed 50 ms Tokio timer: 3.255947791 seconds.
- During backoff: 30 successful reads produced 30 forked tmux launches in 959.333125 ms, with zero control-client launches.

This is directly reproduced worker starvation, not an inferred deployed whole-fleet outage. Other concurrent readers, including live-only readers, can block additional workers on the shared state mutex. Existing synchronous handshake/read costs predate this PR; the new acquisition wait adds to them.

Required correction: keep the contended acquisition and any associated state-mutex waiting off async workers, without weakening cross-process exclusion, sentinel-proven setup, one-start-at-a-time or fallback/backoff behavior. A spawned thread synchronously joined by the worker is not isolation. Promote the timer/launch probe into the existing suite: a short timer must advance while acquisition is pending. R2 checks this fix; no unrelated hardening inventory.

## Requested checks

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Guard lifetime | Correct. The owning `File` is a local in `start`, acquired before launch and held through setup and the sentinel reply. It is never moved into `Live`. Normal returns, `?` errors and panic unwinding drop it; the kernel releases a dead holder's lock. Setup failure destroys `Live` before the guard leaves scope. |
| Reads after timeout | Correct answers via existing fork fallback. `ask:302-304` sets a five-second restart backoff after failure; `stdout:473` still calls `run` for each fallback read. The backoff does not throttle those forks. |
| Runtime-worker isolation | FAIL: R280-001/P280-001, independently reproduced above. |
| Filename confinement | Correct. `attach_lock_path:424-437` maps all characters outside ASCII alphanumeric, dash and underscore to underscore, then joins a fixed dot-file basename. No separator or `..` can escape the root. Sanitization collisions conservatively share a lock. |
| Sweep and launch instrumentation | Correct. The orphan sweep accepts only non-dot regular `*.raw` sinks (`lib.rs:61-76`). The existing control launch is counted only after acquisition; no new launch site. Existing launches still use the resolved executable path. |

The attach lock is a BRAKE, not an outcome policy: removing it permits more concurrent attaches. `destroy-unattached` is preserved. C33 accepts same-user lock holding; no per-seat credential or hostile-local-process defense is requested. Lock creation inherits filesystem permissions/umask rather than setting a private mode; security owns the enclosing-directory access assessment. No personal home paths occur in the six-file diff or this verdict.

## Cost and proof limits

Healthy live reads add no lock work, timer, poll or process. An uncontended start opens one lock file and acquires one flock. A fully contended three-second attempt performs approximately 301 `try_lock` calls, then backs off five seconds: approximately 0.125 attempts/file opens and 37.6 lock attempts per second per affected adapter under continuous demand. This bounded retry is in-process, not a tmux launch loop.

Fallback is demand-driven and has no workload-independent launch-rate ceiling. A tracked matching-tap observer pass performs one global list and three reads per pane; at the unchanged 600 ms cadence the offered load is `(1 + 3N) / 0.6` tmux launches/second per affected daemon, or 401.7/s for 80 panes, plus request-driven reads. Serial launch latency and three-second stalls reduce achieved average throughput; this is an analytic demand budget, not a measured sustained fleet rate. The probe's 30 forks in 0.959 s directly disproves a five-second fork throttle.

No production lock contention, deployment or daemon bounce was performed. A 20-second live machine sample reported 284.4 new processes/s during concurrent fleet/test activity; daemon control-client counter remained 1 across sampling. These are contextual receipts, NOT a before/after deployment comparison.
